Keep every response in English. Tool outputs include controller-owned artifact IDs and

Frozen development lessons:
# Constrained scientific reproduction, revision 3

Your tools enforce a boundary: there is no arbitrary shell, code writing, formula
entry, loader replacement, or selective execution of scientific fragments.
Use list_files and inspect_file to locate instructions and original author files.
Use execute_author with the exact original path. Python, R, shell entry points and
notebooks execute unchanged; for R Markdown, native renders the original document
and r_chunks extracts ALL original R chunks using knitr, without scientific edits.
A failed renderer may justify r_chunks once; a missing scientific dependency or
input is a blocker, not permission to reproduce the calculation yourself.

After a successful execution, inspect its captured stdout or newly generated files.
For notebooks, the controller saves text outputs and figure images under
/results/reproscout-notebook. Use inspect_output to read additional captured lines.
Use view_image for figure questions. Match the exact metric, figure/table, population,
axis range and units to the question. An image with the wrong range is not evidence.
Do not cite manuscript/source prose or old data as a newly computed answer.

Submit finite JSON numbers for numeric contracts, numeric lists for number_list,
and text for string contracts. No numeric strings, units, booleans or NaN. The
submit tool rejects invalid types and unverified non-null evidence; repair the
submission, not the scientific computation. Null with blocker evidence is permitted.
Every non-null citation must come from a successful original execution. That
provenance does not prove your interpretation, so check the evidence before reporting.
Reserve your last two calls to submit. Stop repeated execution/searches once the
blocker is clear. Missing unchanged-computation output must remain null.

Public answer type contracts (null allowed with blocker evidence):
{"q1": "number", "q2": "number"}

23: ```{r analysis}
24: # This chuck calcuates all the results
25: 
26: # Import data
27: filename <- file.path("..", "data", "rec_data_raw.csv")
28: rec <- read.csv(filename, header = T)
29: 
30: # Create separate dataframes for only US and only UK institutions
31: us <- rec %>% filter(country == "us" & !is.na(expenditure_rank))
32: uk <- rec %>% filter(country == "uk" & !is.na(expenditure_rank))
33: 
34: # Create a function to output all the values for the flowchart
35: rec_flowchart <- function(df){ 
36:   flowchart <- data.frame(
37:     item = c(
38:       "Institutions sampled",
39:       "Public forms identified",
40:       "Institutions contacted",
41:       "Public forms identified after contact",
42:       "Private forms provided",
43:       "Forms indicated as not available to share", 
44:       "No response"
45:     ),
46:     count = c(
47:       nrow(df),
48:       sum(df$included == 1 & df$contacted == 0),
49:       sum(df$contacted == T),
50:       sum(df$contacted == 1 & df$form_available == "public", na.rm = T),
51:       sum(sum(df$contacted == 1 & df$form_available == "private", na.rm = T)),
52:       sum(grepl("declined", df$form_available)),
53:       sum(df$form_available == "noreply" | is.na(df$form_available))
54:     )
55:   )
56:   return(flowchart)
57: }
58: 
59: # Create a function to output all the values for the outcomes
60: rec_outcomes <- function(df){
61:   outcomes <- data.frame(
62:     item = c(
63:       "Sample size",
64:       "Justification",
65:       "Calculation",
66:       "Calculation (indirectly)"
67:     ),
68:     count = c(
69:       sum(df$sample_size, na.rm = TRUE),
70:       sum(df$justification, na.rm = TRUE),
71:       sum(df$calculation == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
72:       sum(df$calculation == 99, na.rm = TRUE)
73:     )
74:   )
75:   return(outcomes)
76: }
77: 
78: us_flowchart <- rec_flowchart(us)
79: uk_flowchart <- rec_flowchart(uk)
80: 
81: us_outcomes <- rec_outcomes(us)
82: uk_outcomes <- rec_outcomes(uk)
83: 
84: us_combined <- bind_rows(
85:   rec_flowchart(us),
86:   rec_outcomes(us)
87:   )
88: 
89: uk_combined <- bind_rows(
90:   rec_flowchart(uk),
91:   rec_outcomes(uk)
92:   )
93: 
94: rec_results <- cbind(
95:   us_combined, 
96:   uk_combined$count
97: )
98: ```
